definitions: A feeling of discomfort or shame experienced by an observer when someone else (the target) commits a social blunder or experiences a humiliating situation, even though the observer is not directly involved.
The vicarious experience of embarrassment on behalf of another person.
examples: Her empathic embarrassment was palpable as she watched him trip.
The comedian's act often relied on generating empathic embarrassment in the audience.
He felt a wave of empathic embarrassment for the speaker who forgot their lines.
